overview.text: Dubai is a coastal city in the United Arab Emirates and the main urban center of the Emirate of Dubai, one of the UAE’s seven emirates. On the southeast coast of the Arabian Gulf, the emirate includes sandy shores, desert, and the mountainous region of Hatta. Dubai Creek is a defining feature: its natural harbor helped the city grow as a center for fishing, pearling, and trade, and it divides the historic city into Deira and Bur Dubai. In 1833, the Al Maktoum family established rule in Dubai. Today, the city is a major hub for international business and trade, connecting markets in eastern and western regions.

key_facts.text: Dubai is a city in the UAE; the Emirate of Dubai is one of the UAE’s seven emirates.
The emirate lies on the southeast coast of the Arabian Gulf and includes the Hatta mountain region.
Dubai Creek divides the city into the historic districts of Deira and Bur Dubai.
The Creek’s natural harbor supported fishing, pearling, and trade, helping Dubai grow as a port.
The Al Maktoum family established rule in Dubai in 1833; the city is now a major hub for commerce and business.
